extracted.intended_audience: aspiring mathematicians; mathematics students and academic researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles about what makes a valuable mathematician's life and work, emphasizing original research, talent allocation, motives, and the character of mathematical achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doers versus Talkers
rubrics_metrics.description: The function of a mathematician is to do something, to prove new theorems, to add to mathematics, and not to talk about what he or other mathematicians have done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposition, criticism, appreciation, is work for second-rate minds. The implication: priority is given to original mathematical production rather than commentary or criticism; being primarily an expositor/critic is presented as an inferior role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of Pure Mathematics (Pure versus Applied)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any genuine mathematician must feel that it is not on crude achievements (bridges, steam-engines, dynamos) that the real case for mathematics rests; the mass of mathematical truth is obvious and imposing and its popular reputation is based largely on ignorance and confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the intrinsic, intellectual worth and permanence of mathematical truth over practical utility; defend mathematics by its rational, non-crude merits rather than by sensational applied triumphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work where you can do best (The standard apology)
rubrics_metrics.description: I do what I do because it is the one and only thing that I can do well. Most people can do nothing at all well. Perhaps 5 or 10 percent of men can do something rather well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career choice should be dictated by natural abilities; if one is a real mathematician, one's mathematics will likely be far better than anything else one can do, so one should not surrender chances to exercise that talent in favor of undistinguished work elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics is a young man's game (Young versus Old)
rubrics_metrics.description: No mathematician should ever allow himself to forget that mathematics, more than any other art or science, is a young man's game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples (Newton, Galois, Abel, Ramanujan, Riemann) are cited to support the claim that major mathematical advances are typically initiated early in life; this should inform expectations about timing of peak creativity and career planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic self-assessment (The Humbler Apology)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing that I can do particularly well. I do what I do because it came my way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one genuinely lacks ability to excel, the choice of career matters little; one should be honest about talents and accept the consequences for career significance and ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationalization of mathematics' worth (Rationalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is mathematics unprofitable? Is it useful? Is it harmless? The scale of the universe is large and, if we are wasting our time, the waste of the lives of a few university dons is no such overwhelming catastrophe. What we do may be small, but it has a certain character of permanence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The production of anything of permanent interest (a theorem or a poem) justifies the intellectual life even if it is unprofitable; permanence and contributing something beyond the powers of most men is the core justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary motives for research (Identical Motives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The three most important motives which lead men to prosecute research are intellectual curiosity, professional pride and ambition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These motives are legitimate and indistinguishable across fields; one should not be ashamed of ambition or pride as drivers of genuine scientific or scholarly work. Also guard against the fallacy that benefiting humanity is usually the immediate motive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition to leave something permanent
rubrics_metrics.description: A man's first duty, a young man's at any rate, is to be ambitious. The noblest ambition is that of leaving behind one something of permanent value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambition is portrayed positively as the driving force behind the best work; aiming to create lasting contributions is framed as the highest professional aspiration.
